history.period: 1567 (relocated to Zambaulim); present large temple from 1910
history.summary: The deity was originally housed in a large temple at Mathagam (now Madgaon/Margao), where the Church of the Holy Spirit now stands. During the Portuguese temple-destruction campaign in Sasashti taluka in 1567, the Mahajans of Madgaon shifted the deities (Ramnath, Damodar, Lakshmi-Narayan, Chamundeshwari, Mahakali, Mahesh) to Zambaulim, aided by the Desais of Rivona, who donated land and vatan (still paid today). Tradition says the original Margao temple was consecrated to the memory of a native, Makaji Damodar, who died with his newly married spouse and received divine honours; the Portuguese burnt ten Margao temples, including Damodar's, and built the church on its ruins in 1565. The small Zambaulim temple was replaced by the present large one in 1910. The temple stands on the banks of the Kushavati river, whose waters devotees believe have healing powers. DUPLICATE ROW: this is the same Zambaulim temple as CSV seqs 226, 229 and 232 ('Shri Damodar Temple' variants, handled by other workers) — keep-or-drop decision needed. CSV town 'Sanguem' is the taluka town; the temple is in Zambaulim village, ~5 km from Quepem, so town is corrected to 'Zambaulim'. Coordinates are village-level (geocoder returned street-level match for Zambaulim Road) and should be treated as approximate for the temple precinct.

name: Shree Damodar Temple
town_description: Zambaulim is a village in Sanguem taluka, South Goa, about 5 km from Quepem and 22 km from Margao, on the banks of the Kushavati river. It is a pilgrimage hub for Goud Saraswat Brahmins, hosting several relocated temples on its forested grounds.
tradition: Hindu (Vaishnava; Goud Saraswat Brahmin community temple)

travel.road: ~5 km from Quepem on Zambaulim Road; remote — private cab or own vehicle recommended, public transport is inconvenient

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; the week-long Shigmo–Gulalotsav around Holi (Phalgun Purnima) is the biggest festival
